heard: Space is a silent vacuum, except for one massive cosmic singer. Most people assume sound cannot travel through the total emptiness of space. But the Perseus cluster, 250 million light years away, is filled with hot gas. In 2002, NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory detected real pressure waves rippling through that gas. A supermassive black hole in galaxy NGC 1275 is blowing plasma bubbles, creating a cosmic hum. Astronomers at Cambridge University found this hum is a B-flat note 57 octaves below middle C. A single oscillation of this deep sound wave takes nearly 10 million years to complete. This sound carries the energy of 100 million supernovae, keeping the cluster too hot to form stars. It is a deep, eternal vibration, proving that space is a silent vacuum. You
